name: InsForge (InstaCloud)

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: InsForge (insforge.dev) backend product: InsForge Compute fixed backend sizes Nano 2 vCPU/0.5 GB $0.0067/h ($5/mo) ... 16XL 64 vCPU/128 GB $3.4304/h ($2,560/mo), billed hourly, one per project (API server + Postgres), Pro includes $10/mo credit per org. Custom Compute (own containers on Fly.io machines) is 'billed by usage' with no published rate; Free includes 120 h/month on the default spec. Not priceable as a sandbox; keep flags alt.

modes.label: InstaCloud compute (microVM service, usage-billed)
modes.note: $0.00000772/vCPU-s ($0.027792/vCPU-h) + $0.00000386/GB-s ($0.013896/GB-h), 'You only pay for active CPU and memory' (active = usage basis; exact measurement method unpublished). New services are always-on by default and bill continuously; scale-to-zero is opt-in. Volume $0.0002082/GB-h, object storage $0.00002082/GB-h, egress $0.05/GB. Per-service caps: Free 4 vCPU/4 GB/1 GB volume, Pro and Team 8 vCPU/8 GB (volume 10/50 GB). Same per-second rates as Railway ($20/vCPU-month, $10/GB-month).

plans.name: InstaCloud Free
plans.note: $10 usage credit/month, refreshes monthly; 'Projects pause when credit runs out, and resume next cycle' (hard cap, no overage); up to 4 vCPU/4 GB/1 GB volume per service; 5 services of each type per environment; 5 cron jobs.

plans.name: InstaCloud Pro
plans.note: '$20 / month minimum usage' with '$20 of usage credit per month'; overage on ('projects keep running'); up to 8 vCPU/8 GB/10 GB volume per service; 25 services of each type per environment; vertical scaling and replicas; 100 cron jobs.

plans.name: InstaCloud Team
plans.note: 'Usage billed on top of the monthly platform fee'; up to 8 vCPU/8 GB/50 GB volume per service; 100 services of each type per environment; higher limits on request; SOC 2, SSO; HIPAA paid add-on; 1,000 cron jobs.

plans.name: InstaCloud Enterprise
plans.note: Custom usage credit and resource limits, HIPAA BAAs, SLA.

caveats: Pro $25 monthly/$20 annual with $10 InsForge Compute credits; backend compute is specifically API+Postgres, NOT Custom Compute. Public table 4vCPU/16GB $0.2144/h describes backend project server. Do not price arbitrary containers at it. Custom Compute has separate usage billing, current rate unresolved; free 120h default custom compute. Backend bandwidth 250GB then $0.09/GB.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

insforge.dev pricing contradiction: pricing page says the $10 InsForge Compute credit 'Does not apply' to Custom Compute, but docs.insforge.dev/pricing FAQ says Custom Compute on Pro comes with '$10 of InsForge Compute credits to offset it'. InsForge Custom Compute has no published per-hour rate (runs on Fly.io machines). InsForge Free projects pause after 1 week of inactivity.

InstaCloud compute: new services are always-on by default ('New compute services are always-on and never scale to zero') and bill continuously; scale-to-zero is opt-in; volume-backed services cold-stop instead of suspend; since 2026-09-26 outbound traffic also keeps a scale-to-zero service awake (so an agent calling a model keeps billing). Root disk is rebuilt on every wake; only the volume persists.

fleet.verification: Free backend tier advertised without a credit card.
fleet.tiers: InstaCloud: Free 5 / Pro 25 / Team 100 services of each type per environment; per-service max 4 vCPU/4 GB (Free), 8 vCPU/8 GB (Pro/Team); 'Higher limits on request' on Team; replicas ('insta compute scale') on paid plans only. InsForge backend: Free 2 dedicated backend projects; Custom Compute 120 h/month free.
fleet.notes: Do not equate 2 backend projects with arbitrary Custom Compute machine concurrency: current pricing separates the two and gives 120 free Custom Compute hours without an aggregate running-machine cap. New-account fleet quota and review time remain unknown.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A suspended service is skipped instead of deployed: a deploy would invalidate the RAM snapshot suspension exists to preserve, so it is left untouched and reported with reason `suspended`.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: idle timeout on services opted into scale-to-zero (compute/overview: "Opt one into scale-to-zero and an idle machine suspends until the next request wakes it in seconds."); memory included (RAM snapshot, Fly-style suspend). Default is always-on (no suspend). Not for volume-backed services: "Volume-backed services stop (cold wake) instead of suspending" and the root disk is rebuilt on every wake. Hosted platform only; self-hosted OSS stops containers instead.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: | Compute `/data` volume | Same size, empty (self-hosted InstaCloud OSS forks the volume files instead) |
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint endpoint in the full OpenAPI reference. Closest: on-demand `insta compute suspend` (RAM preserved, resumes in place; = pause/resume, cannot fork) and branches, which clone Postgres (copy-on-write) and buckets but recreate compute from the image with an EMPTY volume on the hosted platform. Postgres has its own branching; no machine snapshots.

harness_api.quote: Under the hood the agent runs the [insta CLI](/reference/cli/overview), which you can also drive by hand.
harness_api.note: InstaCloud is infrastructure driven BY a coding agent running elsewhere (CLI, MCP server, skills); no API to launch/drive Claude Code/Codex inside a compute service. Only a generic one-shot exec endpoint ("Run a one-shot command inside a compute service's machine").

ingress_rules.quote: Services reach each other over their public HTTPS URLs. Compute listens on one HTTP port and a raw TCP port cannot be exposed at all
ingress_rules.note: Each compute service gets one public HTTPS URL on one chosen HTTP port; no private network, no auth-gated/tokenized URLs or IP allowlists documented. The public/private access toggle (set-service-access, MCP insta_set_service_access) is documented for storage buckets and managed databases, not compute. Custom domains available.

guest_firewall.quote: Compute services now run as full Linux VMs with cgroups and root, so your agent can install Docker inside its own compute and use it the way it would on a laptop
guest_firewall.note: Sep 11, 2026 changelog; the example installs iptables and runs dockerd inside the microVM, which requires working netfilter. Not an explicit 'nftables supported' statement.

secret_proxy.quote: Secrets and credential bindings (`insta secrets bind`) are injected as environment variables at deploy time.
secret_proxy.note: User secrets and bound service credentials land in the container env; no outbound credential-injecting proxy. (InsForge's separate BaaS has a model gateway for app frontends, not a sandbox secret proxy.)

volume_attach.quote: Need disk that survives restarts? Attach a persistent `/data` volume:
volume_attach.note: One volume per compute service, default 1 GiB on any plan, larger paid and plan-capped (Free 1 GB, Pro 10, Team 50 per card); mount path selectable since 2026-09-24; $0.0002082/GB-h. Volume forces cold stop instead of suspend.

volume_shared.quote: Compute services without a persistent volume can now run multiple replicas in the same region.
volume_shared.note: A volume belongs to a single-machine service (no replicas with a volume); no shared/network filesystem. S3-compatible storage buckets exist but are accessed via API, not mounted.

isolation.quote: Each service runs in its own microVM — hardware-level isolation rather than a shared-kernel container, which is what makes it safe to run agent-built code next to everything else.
isolation.note: Docs say 'microVM' with hardware-level isolation and describe a home-grown 'microvm plane' (distinct from 'legacy Fly'), but never name the underlying hypervisor; firecracker is the de-facto standard for this class of microVM and the closest fit to the field taxonomy.

image_oci.quote: From a prebuilt image. Skip the build entirely — exactly one of a directory or `--image` per deploy: insta deploy --image ghcr.io/acme/api:v3
image_oci.note: Deploys any OCI image from any registry, or builds one remotely from a Dockerfile.

nested_virt.quote: Each service runs in its own microVM — hardware-level isolation rather than a shared-kernel container
nested_virt.note: No mention of /dev/kvm or nested virtualization anywhere in the docs, CLI reference, or changelog; the Docker-inside-compute changelog entry runs a userspace dockerd (via cgroups/root), not a nested-VM emulator. Derived, not explicitly stated.

desktop.quote: InstaCloud provides the three basic primitives, rebuilt on those terms: database (real Postgres), storage (S3-compatible buckets), and compute (containers, run in microVMs on the hosted platform).
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (generic container/backend PaaS, no graphical desktop).

browser.quote: InstaCloud provides the three basic primitives, rebuilt on those terms: database (real Postgres), storage (S3-compatible buckets), and compute (containers, run in microVMs on the hosted platform).
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No managed/real browser product; the only 'browser' mentions in docs are the human's own browser used to sign into the console.

computer_use.quote: InstaCloud provides the three basic primitives, rebuilt on those terms: database (real Postgres), storage (S3-compatible buckets), and compute (containers, run in microVMs on the hosted platform).
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no screenshot/click desktop-driving API; the product is backend compute/storage/database infrastructure driven by CLI, MCP, and REST.

anti_bot.quote: InstaCloud provides the three basic primitives, rebuilt on those terms: database (real Postgres), storage (S3-compatible buckets), and compute (containers, run in microVMs on the hosted platform).
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no browser/stealth product).

captcha_solving.quote: InstaCloud provides the three basic primitives, rebuilt on those terms: database (real Postgres), storage (S3-compatible buckets), and compute (containers, run in microVMs on the hosted platform).
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no browser/CAPTCHA product).

egress_ip_type.quote: Each service runs in its own microVM — hardware-level isolation rather than a shared-kernel container
egress_ip_type.note: Standard cloud microVM egress; no residential/mobile IP product mentioned anywhere, and no static/dedicated outbound IP is documented (see static_egress_ip).

snapshot.quote: A suspended service is skipped instead of deployed: a deploy would invalidate the RAM snapshot suspension exists to preserve, so it is left untouched and reported with reason `suspended`.
snapshot.note: Suspend/resume preserves a RAM snapshot of a compute service (memory + disk), auto-triggered by scale-to-zero idle. There is no separate on-demand disk-only snapshot API (see feature_evidence.snapshot_on_demand in the card: false); branching clones Postgres/bucket data but rebuilds compute from the image with an empty volume, not a memory snapshot.

fork.quote: Give every agent task its own branch: a copy-on-write database with the parent's data, a forked bucket, and a running copy of the app at its own URL.
fork.note: 'insta branch create' forks the current branch (or --from another) into a new branch with its own compute/db/bucket.

fork_running.quote: A live URL from the start. Branch compute comes up running the parent's image, so the agent can see the app working before its first deploy.
fork_running.note: Branching does not require stopping the source: the parent keeps serving traffic on its own branch/URL while the new branch is created from its image.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: | Compute `/data` volume | Same size, empty (self-hosted InstaCloud OSS forks the volume files instead) |
memory_snapshot_fork.note: A branch's compute service is recreated from the parent's deployed image (cold start), not cloned with its running process/memory state; only Postgres and the bucket are copy-on-write.

live_resize.quote: every machine-facing change lands as one reconfigure per machine (one restart, not one per field)
live_resize.note: Raising/lowering a compute service's CPU/RAM ceiling (`insta compute limits` / set-service-limits) is a machine-facing change and triggers a restart, so it is not a live resize without interruption.

agent_harnesses.quote: Under the hood the agent runs the [insta CLI](/reference/cli/overview), which you can also drive by hand.
agent_harnesses.note: InstaCloud installs a CLI/MCP-server/skill so an existing coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) on the developer's own machine can drive InstaCloud — it does not preinstall or offer coding-agent harnesses as templates running inside its compute sandboxes.

own_agent_api.quote: InstaCloud is the cloud infrastructure built from the ground up to serve agents.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. InstaCloud is infrastructure driven by an agent (yours), not a first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent of its own.

lang_python.quote: An image, its environment, and a listen port: * Image — built remotely from your Dockerfile on `insta deploy .`, or supplied prebuilt with `--image`.
lang_python.note: Compute runs whatever container/image you bring (a Dockerfile or prebuilt OCI image); no Python runtime is provided out of the box unless your own image includes it, and there is no first-party Python code-exec SDK.

lang_node.quote: An image, its environment, and a listen port: * Image — built remotely from your Dockerfile on `insta deploy .`, or supplied prebuilt with `--image`.
lang_node.note: Same as lang_python: Node.js has to be in the customer's own image/Dockerfile; the `insta` CLI itself requires Node.js on the developer's machine (not inside the sandbox), and there is no first-party Node code-exec SDK for the compute service.

public_ipv4.quote: Services reach each other over their public HTTPS URLs. Compute listens on one HTTP port and a raw TCP port cannot be exposed at all
public_ipv4.note: Compute services are reached via a shared public HTTPS URL/router, not a per-machine public IPv4. (A dedicated public IP at <app>.fly.dev is documented only for opting a managed database like Redis/MySQL/MongoDB into direct internet access, not for compute.)

egress_allowlist.quote: No private network — Services reach each other over their public HTTPS URLs.
egress_allowlist.note: No outbound allow/deny-list, no-internet mode, or security-group egress control is documented anywhere in the docs, API reference, or OpenAPI spec; the only 'allow/deny' concepts found are agent-governance rules over API operations, not network egress.

egress_http_rules.quote: No private network — Services reach each other over their public HTTPS URLs.
egress_http_rules.note: No method/path-level egress control is documented; same evidence as egress_allowlist.

static_egress_ip.quote: Run any container in a microVM, always on or scaling to zero.
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP is documented for compute services anywhere in the docs, changelog, or OpenAPI spec.

gpu.quote: InstaCloud provides the three basic primitives, rebuilt on those terms: database (real Postgres), storage (S3-compatible buckets), and compute (containers, run in microVMs on the hosted platform).
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No GPU instance type, size, or pricing is mentioned anywhere in the docs, pricing page, or OpenAPI spec.

windows.quote: A compute service runs your container — web app, API, worker — in an isolated microVM with its own URL.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Compute runs Linux containers (Docker images); no Windows machine option is documented.

macos.quote: A compute service runs your container — web app, API, worker — in an isolated microVM with its own URL.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Linux-container microVMs only; no macOS machine option is documented.

byoc.quote: Run the InstaCloud runtime on your own machine: one daemon over Docker, the same CLI, the same URL shape.
byoc.note: InstaCloud offers self-hosting (open-source, self_host: true) that you install and operate yourself on your own box, not a provider-managed deployment into your own cloud account (BYOC).

eu_data_residency.note: The live regions API lists 'Europe (Frankfurt)' as a selectable deployment region for postgres/compute services.

max_session_h.quote: New compute services are always-on and never scale to zero, on every branch.
max_session_h.note: A compute service is not time-boxed; it runs (always-on or scale-to-zero-and-wake) until you explicitly stop it. No maximum session/runtime duration is documented.

private_network.quote: No private network ... Services reach each other over their public HTTPS URLs. Compute listens on one HTTP port and a raw TCP port cannot be exposed at all, so a container speaking a wire protocol of its own runs fine and nothing reaches it, inside the project or outside. Use the managed Postgres, Redis, MySQL and MongoDB types for that.
private_network.note: Official docs devote a dedicated 'No private network' limitations section confirming there is no inter-service private networking; only public HTTPS URLs, and raw TCP cannot be exposed at all. This settles the card's existing 'no' with a direct first-party source.

arm64.quote: From a directory, a Dockerfile, an image, or GitHub to a running service. ... A deploy puts a container on a compute service and prints its URL.
arm64.note: The hosted InstaCloud platform's compute/deploy docs never mention an architecture choice or ARM machine option for compute services (remote builds and image deploys are described with no arch flag). The only documented arm64/aarch64 support in the whole docs corpus is for the self-hosted InstaCloud OSS daemon and its bundled templates (`ghcr.io/insforge/instacloud` published for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64; install requires x86_64 or aarch64), which is a separate self-managed product from the hosted compute service this card models. No hosted-platform ARM compute size/region is documented, so treated as not offered on the hosted product.

usage_api.quote: GET /projects/{projectId}/usage returns ProjectUsage with dimensions (ram, cpu, volume, storage, egress) and totalCostUsd per project; /orgs/{orgId}/usage returns per-project breakdown with cost. DimensionUsage includes quantity, unit, and costUsd.
